activities.anchor: By 750 CE the caliphate stretched from Spain
activities.caption: pair each asset with its record
activities.name: goldenStageMatch

config.prompt: The stage, c. 750 — pair each asset with what it gave the scholars:

pairs.right: founded in 762 as the Abbasid capital — perhaps half a million people
claimed libraries of hundreds of thousands of volumes
the language of scripture — prestigious and universal
taxed and legally subordinate, but present in the libraries — Greek into Syriac into Arabic

config.why: One language of learning, one coinage zone and trade routes from Córdoba to Samarkand: science had a market, a language and a transport network — the three things the classical world never fully assembled.

activities.anchor: funded a systematic hunt for the world's knowledge
activities.caption: walk a manuscript into Baghdad
activities.name: goldenProcureOrder

config.prompt: A Greek text heads for the House of Wisdom — order the pipeline, first step first:
items: An embassy seeks Greek manuscripts from Byzantium
Persian administrative texts, Indian tables and Chinese technology arrive by every route
Rendered from Greek into Syriac — the craft passing father to son
Syriac into Arabic, by the paid teams of translators
Corrected, extended and shelved as a single-language corpus
config.why: Procurement, not miracle: Hunayn ibn Ishaq reportedly paid his weights in gold for rare Galenic manuscripts, and the caliphs' mixed motives — prestige, piety and utility — kept the embassies funded. What the Renaissance called 'recovering the ancients' was completed by 900 CE.

activities.anchor: A warehouse does not improve its stock
activities.caption: find the line the myth would love
activities.name: goldenWarehouseSpot

config.prompt: One line of this summary is the copying-and-storing myth speaking — click it:
lines: Ptolemy's tables were challenged with new observations.
Galen's medicine was reorganised and taught in hospitals.
Algebra was a discipline the Greeks never had.
The translators corrected, systematised and extended what they copied.
The translators merely stored the Greek texts unchanged until Europe was ready.
config.correction: Preservation was the smallest part of the movement: this civilisation improved its stock.
config.why: New observations against Ptolemy, Galen reorganised in hospitals, algebra invented as a genre — correction and extension, the opposite of warehousing.

activities.anchor: Two mathematical events anchor the era
activities.caption: file each tool by where it came from
activities.name: goldenMathBuckets

config.prompt: Golden Age mathematics — file each piece by its origin:

items.label: algebra as a method — classify equation types, solve generically
decimal fractions pushed to remarkable precision by al-Kashi
the Law of Sines in its full form
nine digits and zero, with place value
geometric justification in the Euclidean manner

config.why: Algebra and mature trigonometry were genuine inventions of method; the numerals were borrowed and argued for — the contribution was adoption, explanation and development. Fibonacci's Liber Abaci (1202) imported the settled technology into Europe, where Roman numerals took two more centuries to fall.

activities.anchor: Islamic medicine institutionalised what the Greeks had theorised
activities.caption: scrub the bimaristan centuries
activities.name: goldenMedTimeline

events.title: Baghdad's Audidi hospital
events.text: The bimaristan spreads from here to Damascus, Cairo and Córdoba — wards by disease, teaching, licensed physicians, endowed as waqf.

events.title: al-Razi dies
events.text: Rhazes ran Baghdad's hospital, wrote the encyclopedic Al-Hawi and distinguished smallpox from measles — clinical observation as method.

events.title: Cataract suction, documented
events.text: Ammar ibn Ali al-Mawsili describes cataract suction with a hollow needle — surgical craft documented, taught and regulated.

events.title: Ibn Sina dies
events.text: Avicenna's Canon compresses medicine drug-by-drug, disease-by-disease — the European medical textbook until the 1600s.

events.title: The Canon, still printing
events.text: Montpellier and Louvain are still printing Avicenna in the 1650s — six centuries after his death.

config.root: Cairo, c. 1020. Two Greek theories of vision are on the table: Plato's ray shooting out of the eye, Aristotle's form received whole. You are Ibn al-Haytham.

start.text: How should the question be settled?

choices.label: Side with Plato — the eye emits the ray
choices.feedback: A thousand years of authority — and nothing tested.

choices.label: Side with Aristotle — the form is received whole
choices.feedback: Another inherited position, defended by argument alone.

choices.label: Design a decisive test
choices.feedback: Doubt inherited authority; state the question; build the experiment.

plato.text: The emission theory answers to no observation and explains nothing new.

aristotle.text: Every claim still rests on argument, not demonstration.

darkroom.text: In the camera obscura — the earliest documented controlled optical laboratory — you demonstrate that light travels in straight lines from every point of an object into the eye, and that vision is the eye's reception of that light.

choices.label: Report the results for others to verify
choices.feedback: Demonstration, not argument, decides the case.

report.text: The Book of Optics reaches Latin: Roger Bacon, Witelo and Kepler read it — Kepler solves the image-formation problem Ibn al-Haytham left open.

config.why: Doubt inherited authority, state the question, design a decisive test, report results for verification — a working method statement around 1020, centuries before seventeenth-century Europe.

activities.caption: drag the divider — the writing surface decides
activities.name: goldenPaperCompare

config.prompt: One craft — learned, tradition says, from Chinese prisoners taken at the Talas river (751) — reached Baghdad by 793. Drag the divider:

before.label: Parchment and scrolls
before.text: Expensive and unwieldy: a book culture that cannot scale.

after.label: Paper from 793
after.text: Cheap, foldable, mass-producible: private libraries in the thousands of volumes, copying shops as endowed businesses, scholarly argument carried by post across a continent.

config.why: Trade routes were knowledge routes — merchants carried books beside spices, pilgrims carried ideas, refugees carried libraries — and the waqf endowment financed mosques, madrasas, hospitals and libraries as the era's research-funding model.

activities.anchor: Astronomy was the Golden Age's big-budget science
activities.caption: call the count — Samarkand's sky
activities.name: goldenObsEstimate

config.prompt: Ulugh Beg's Samarkand observatory (1420s) produced a star catalogue — roughly how many stars?
config.why: Over 1,000 stars — the most accurate catalogue of its century, built on the era's greatest mural quadrant.
config.context: Maragha (1259) ran a professional staff and, by report, a library of 400,000 volumes; al-Tusi's 'Tusi couple' let planetary models drop Ptolemy's awkward equant.
